concept_name: From Form Fields to Law Pages — Make Gallery Previews Look Like Actual Trust Documents
problem_statement: The two gallery cards on the homepage are the visitor's first encounter with what FreeTrustDocs produces, yet their embedded sheet previews display form-field UI — labeled entries like 'Trust name [Trust Name]' and 'Trustee [Trustee Name]' — which reads as a database record or wizard step, not as a finished legal document. This directly undermines the page's credibility as a legal-document tool. The showcase section below already uses a convincing '.doc-sheet' silhouette with justified text lines, preamble, section count, and a notary block, proving the visual language exists but is not being reused where it matters most: inside the selector itself. The hero H1 is also undersized at 2.5rem for a legal product that needs to project authority, and the 'FTD / DOCUMENT SYSTEM' tech ribbon speaks to developers rather than someone shopping for a trust document.
proposed_changes: Replace the form-field layout inside .gallery-card-sheet (currently two labeled rows: 'Trust name [ Trust Name ]' and 'Trustee [ Trustee Name ]') with a genuine document-silhouette preview: the existing card title and rule on top, then four lines of varying-length gray placeholder prose text (no labels, no brackets, simulating legal language), then a signature block at bottom reusing the existing .doc-notary and .doc-notary-line classes. This is the single highest-leverage change — it answers the visitor's core question ('what will the output look like?') at the exact moment they are choosing which document to generate.

Increase .gallery-card-sheet min-height to ~160px and normalize its padding to var(--space-md) on all sides. The current sheet area is only ~60px tall — enough for two labeled fields but not enough to convey a document page. A taller sheet gives the prose lines and signature block room to breathe and reads as a miniature legal page rather than an info card.

Scale the hero H1 up from 2.5rem to a clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3rem) with line-height tightened to 1.15. Legal tools project trust through typographic weight and presence. The current 2.5rem headline, after accounting for the header bar, tech ribbon, and generous top padding, occupies less than 30% of the hero viewport — leaving the space feeling empty rather than authoritative.

Reduce .ftd-tech-ribbon opacity from 0.62 to 0.35 and increase its letter-spacing to 0.2em, or relocate it from above the hero to flush against the bottom of the site-header border. The ribbon currently reads as a dev-console status line ('FTD / DOCUMENT SYSTEM' in monospace with dot separators), which communicates 'tech demo' rather than 'professional legal tool.'

Add a small scroll-key SVG watermark (the existing logo-mark at 20px, 20% opacity in var(--color-accent)) to the top-right corner of the sheet preview area on .gallery-card--selected. The current selected state is a green border plus 4% background tint — functional but visually underwhelming. A contextual document icon reinforces that each card represents an actual producible document, not just a tab.
rationale: Every proposed change targets one core gap: the homepage currently looks like a SaaS lead-capture page with a form-like preview when it should look like the front cover of a legal document library. The single highest-leverage fix is replacing the form-field mockups in the gallery cards with genuine document silhouettes — this alone shifts the page from 'generic tool' to 'crafted legal product.' The remaining changes (type scale, ribbon, card proportions, selection indicator) are supporting adjustments that ensure the new visual direction is executed at full fidelity rather than being constrained by the existing layout's assumptions about what the preview area contains. The brand's style guide (forest green, bronze, cream, Crimson Pro, engraving aesthetic, no gradients, no photography) is already strong and consistent; the issue is not the system but how it is applied in this one interactive component.
